newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off on Nikkei recovery.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off on Nikkei recovery.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures came under pressure late on Tuesday after the Nikkei share average wiped out most of its early losses.
"Everything is correlated right now between the Euroyen, JGBs and the Nikkei," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.

He said September Euroyen had seen good buying interest around the 99.30 level initially, but it then came under pressure alongside JGBs when the Nikkei made an unexpected recovery in afternoon trade.
"The JGBs came under continuous selling in London after the Nikkei made a miraculous recovery," he said.
The Nikkei share average ended 25.66 points lower at 18,093.13 after falling as low as 17,545.52.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.29 at 1105 GMT against its IMM close at 99.32. December was at 99.15 against 99.18.
"My near-term target for September is the 99.40 level," said the trader, adding that the contract looked supported at 99.28.
March JGBs ended at 125.57 against their previous 125.66.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed after trading in a one-tick range ahead of the U.S. Consumer Price Index and retail sales data for December, due at 1330 GMT.
"I would like to stay short in Eurodollars. I'm still bearish on them compared with Euroyen," said the trader.
Dealers said there were growing expectations the Federal Reserve would move to raise short-term U.S. interest rates in the coming months.
The market showed no reaction to a speech by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan, speaking in Belgium, urged central banks not to take risks with inflation and said the best monetary policy was a steady course with the right amount of restraint.
